duplicate_rule: duplicate global directives are not rejected merely for duplication; OpenSSH first-obtained-value semantics are adjudicated by the effective sshd output, while the source-exact main-file no remains mandatory
effective_rule: sshd -T -C user=root,host=localhost,addr=127.0.0.1 -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config must emit exactly one effective value for the control's key (lowercase keyword) and it must be no
error_value_contract: Every ERROR wire value is a stable <domain>:<reason> code; literal - is reserved for non-error absence such as NOT_FOUND.
include_rule: active Include directives are recursively inspected in explicit lexical pathname order; each included file inherits the containing file's current Match scope and cannot clobber that scope on return; absolute patterns stay absolute and relative patterns are rooted at /etc/ssh; no-match patterns are allowed; glob discovery/sort failures or newline-containing matched pathnames yield ERROR
key_rule: one control per key; only the control's own key is inspected; other directives never satisfy it
match_rule: each included file starts with the containing file's current Match scope and scope changes inside that included file do not leak back to the containing file; a Match-scope directive with value no is harmless; a Match-scope non-no value is classified ERROR because v1 does not claim exhaustive proof that the conditional branch can never apply

missing_behavior.note: absence is observable technology absence, not source compliance

parser_rule: for inspected sshd keywords, OpenSSH-like whitespace or one optional = separates keyword/value; quoted and escaped arguments are tokenized, CR line endings are normalized, and # starts a comment only at a new token boundary; include cycles, non-regular/symlink/unreadable included files, malformed relevant directives, tokenization/traversal/dependency errors, or parser-depth overflow yield ERROR rather than a guessed PASS; raw NUL is rejected before line parsing, and CR is accepted only as canonical CRLF immediately before LF
source_rule: the main /etc/ssh/sshd_config must contain an active global directive for the control's key (PermitEmptyPasswords, PermitRootLogin or PasswordAuthentication) with semantic value no; a managed drop-in alone does not satisfy the source wording
syntax_rule: sshd -t -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config must succeed before compliance can be asserted
